anomalies.observed: On the CAN0 controller U8 (MCP2515-xSO) the SPI data labels are attached the wrong way round: the net labelled CAN_CIPO is wired to pin 14 (SI, the peripheral's serial input) and CAN_COPI is wired to pin 15 (SO, the peripheral's serial output). The CAN1 controller U9 in the same block shows the opposite (and correct) order, CAN_CIPO to pin 15 / CAN_COPI to pin 14, matching the serial SPI chips (e.g. U14 SC16IS752 with SERIAL_COPI on pin 11 = A1/SI and SERIAL_CIPO on pin 12 = SO).
anomalies.expected: Per the schematic's own note, "COPI ''Controller Out, Peripheral In'' CIPO ''Controller In, Peripheral Out''", the controller-out line (CAN_COPI, from the CM4 MOSI) must drive the MCP2515 serial input SI (pin 14) and the controller-in line (CAN_CIPO, to the CM4 MISO) must come from SO (pin 15). U9 and the serial SPI chips are wired this way; U8 is not.

evidence.quote: CAN_CIPO 14 / CAN_COPI 15 ... SI 14 / SO 15 (CAN BUS block, U8 MCP2515-xSO)
CAN_CIPO 15 / CAN_COPI 14 ... SI 14 / SO 15 (second CAN controller U9)
SPI Naming Note: COPI ''Controller Out, Peripheral In'' CIPO ''Controller In, Peripheral Out''

anomalies.impact: The CM4's SPI MOSI/MISO are crossed at the CAN0 controller, so the processor can never initialise or exchange frames with U8. The CAN0 bus (one of the two buses intended for the Odrive motor controllers) is therefore dead, while CAN1 still works, giving asymmetric motor-control communications.

parsed.summary: The design otherwise matches the specification (16 MHz CAN crystals, SN74LVC1G07 e-stop buffers, LTC4412 ideal-diode, WS2812B chain, ISL54222 mux, 120R CAN terminations, correct USB-C CC resistors, etc.), but the CAN0 controller U8 appears to have its SPI data pair crossed (CAN_CIPO on SI/pin 14, CAN_COPI on SO/pin 15) whereas the identical CAN1 controller U9 and the serial SPI chips use the correct COPI-to-SI / CIPO-to-SO orientation, which would disable CAN0.
